definition: The interest rate used to calculate the present value of future cash flows. A higher discount rate reduces the present value of an invoice's expected returns.
The length of time remaining until an invoice or financial instrument matures and the principal is repaid.
The right of an investor to claim repayment from the original seller if the debtor defaults. Full-recourse invoices reduce credit risk for investors.
The order in which proceeds from an asset are distributed to investors. Senior tranches are paid first, junior tranches absorb losses first.
The annualised return an investor earns on an invoice, expressed as a percentage of the amount invested.
A slice of an investment structured to carry different risk and return profiles. Senior tranches have priority repayment; junior tranches offer higher yields.
An asset pledged by a borrower to secure a loan or investment. If the borrower defaults, the lender may seize the collateral to recover funds.
Know Your Customer — the process of verifying the identity of investors and issuers to comply with financial regulations and prevent fraud.
Anti-Money Laundering — a set of laws, regulations, and procedures that detect and prevent the disguising of illegally obtained funds as legitimate income.
A numerical rating that represents the creditworthiness of an issuer based on their repayment history, outstanding obligations, and financial health.
